name: Rib removal

card.summary: Elective rib removal is a surgery that removes the lower floating ribs to narrow the waist and create a more pronounced hourglass shape.
card.aka: Waist reduction surgery; floating rib removal; ant waist surgery
card.note: Major elective surgery; published aesthetic series are very small.

quick.overview:
Rib removal, also called floating rib resection, takes out the 11th and 12th ribs, and sometimes the 10th, so that the waist sits narrower relative to the hips. The aim is a smaller waist and a lower waist-to-hip ratio.

A 2023 case series from Taiwan reported a mean waist-to-hip ratio drop from 0.78 to 0.72 in five patients. A newer technique that remodels the ribs without removing them has been pooled in a 2026 meta-analysis.
quick.how: The procedure is performed by plastic surgeons under anaesthesia, sometimes as an outpatient operation, and is used alone or with liposuction or fat grafting.
quick.risks: As an elective major surgery it carries general operative risks. The published aesthetic series are small and report few complications, and the rib-remodelling meta-analysis found low pneumothorax, infection and asymmetry rates.

lead: Elective rib removal is a body-contouring surgery in which the lowest ribs are removed to narrow the waist [1][3]. It is associated with the hourglass ideal and with people who pursue extreme waist reduction.

Historically, stories claimed that Victorian-era women or performers such as Polaire had ribs removed for tighter corsetry; historians and Snopes treat these accounts as rumours without documentation [2]. A modern case is Swedish model Pixee Fox, who in 2015 reportedly had ribs 10 to 12 removed by Dr Barry Eppley in Indiana at a reported cost of $9,000 [2].
Aesthetic literature is small. A 2023 series reported on resection of the 11th and 12th ribs, and surgeons have also developed methods that fracture and reshape the ribs without removal [3][4][5].

chain: Surgically remove or remodel lower floating ribs
Narrower waist and lower waist-to-hip ratio
angle.text: Rib removal directly changes the lower ribcage, narrowing the waist for a more hourglass silhouette. It is a surgical option people consider for waist reduction beyond what diet, training or liposuction achieve.

paras: The floating ribs do not attach to the sternum, which is why they are the ones considered for aesthetic resection [3]. In Pixee Fox's reported case, ribs 10 to 12 and some attached muscle were removed [2].

In 1931 corset-maker Rosa Binner alleged that Polaire had a rib removed in the 1890s; Valerie Steele and Lynne Kutsche found no evidence of the Victorian procedure, and John E. Sherman told Vogue in 2000 it was possible in theory but undocumented in the literature [2].

A 2023 retrospective series of five patients at a Taiwan institute who underwent 11th and 12th rib resection found mean waist-to-hip ratio falling from 0.78 to 0.72, with no adverse events and all patients satisfied [3]. A 2021 paper described a minimally invasive method of narrowing the waist by osteotomy and green-stick fracture of the 11th and 12th ribs without removing them [4]. A 2026 meta-analysis of four studies and 318 patients on rib remodelling without resection reported a waistline reduction of about 8.6 cm at three months and low rates of pneumothorax, hemothorax and infection [5].
Rib removal for aesthetic purposes is a major surgical procedure, and the published aesthetic series are too small to define complication rates [3][5].
